story.head: The Kings shut down the dangerous stuff, the Sharks don’t
paras: The Sharks won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-4 in overtime in San Jose on Oct 3. The Sharks (7-8-1) lost 2-1 to Calgary on Monday, and the Kings (4-7-2) lost 3-2 to Buffalo on Saturday. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Sharks fifth (tied for 22nd in the NHL) and the Kings seventh (30th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Sharks’ record (.469) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.382), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Kings have played better than their record (.385) says: their chances are worth about .591, and their finishing has held them back.
This season, the Kings have been outscored 45-36, but only 23-20 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 15-10.

The Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (3rd lowest), ice the puck a lot (32nd) and give up a lot of shots (30th). The Kings leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest), lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd lowest) and take a lot of low-quality shots (31st). The Kings keep dangerous shots away, but the Sharks give up a lot of them.

Macklin Celebrini (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 14 GP) is carrying the Sharks’ offense, and Will Smith (6 G / 4 A / 10 P in 16 GP) has a team-high six goals. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin (8 G / 5 A / 13 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven goals in seven games against San Jose since 2023-24. Brandt Clarke (3 G / 7 A / 10 P in 13 GP) isn’t far behind.
Yaroslav Askarov (4-6-0 / .901 SV% in 10 GS) is expected to start for San Jose, and Darcy Kuemper (4-3-1 / .878 SV% in 8 GS) for Los Angeles.
